## Overview

Adds a fault slice (`FAULTS=1`) to the P2P KV-offload e2e matrix: one of two p2p sources stalls, is killed and restarted, or is removed, while a decoder keeps pulling from both. Requested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61846#issuecomment-6410237963 and follows the cases of the #63602 reproducer.

**Stacked on #61846**: only the last commit (`6cfc3e21d8`) is new here. Review that commit; the rest lands with #61846.

## Claims

- New `FAULTS=1` slice in `config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh` with three cases on Llama-3.2-1B, p2p mode (`remote_kv_source`), 3 GPUs:
  | case | fault on source 0, 10 s into the run |
  |---|---|
  | `stall` | SIGSTOP its processes for 30 s, then SIGCONT |
  | `kill` | SIGKILL, then restart on the same ports |
  | `remove` | SIGTERM, left down |
- `p2p_fault_check.py` asserts time bounds and recovery rather than gsm8k:
  - every decoder request returns 200
  - requests naming the faulted source end within 15 s, and once the fault is detected (from 12 s on) take ≤ 2 s at the median, so the decoder prefills locally instead of waiting
  - pulls from the healthy source keep hitting (≥ 90%) within 5 s, so the fault does not freeze the decoder's p2p control plane
  - after SIGCONT or the restart, ≥ 50% of pulls from the faulted source hit again
- The `stall` case fails on current main and passes with #64501.

## Validation

4× H200, one host, TCP (no RDMA), branch at merge base `fa3b9d1377` with a precompiled wheel. Each case run once via `FAULT_CASE=<case> NUM_PREFILL_INSTANCES=2 bash tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/run_accuracy_test.sh`; the whole slice is `FAULTS=1 bash tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh`, about 7 minutes.

Requests naming the faulted source during the fault (n ≈ 55–60 per row), and pulls from the healthy source:

| arm | case | result | faulted source p50 / max | healthy source pulled, max | faulted source pulled after recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | stall | **FAIL** | 16.85 s / 30.04 s | 60/60, 0.07 s | 43/51 |
| main | kill | pass | 0.01 s / 0.05 s | 58/58, 0.06 s | 51/51 |
| main | remove | pass | 0.01 s / 0.02 s | 61/61, 0.03 s | – |
| + #64501 | stall | pass | 0.01 s / 7.08 s | 60/60, 0.06 s | 41/51 |
| + #64501 | kill | pass | 0.01 s / 0.04 s | 58/58, 0.06 s | 51/51 |
| + #64501 | remove | pass | 0.01 s / 0.02 s | 61/61, 0.04 s | – |

The main `stall` failure:

```
fault faulted: n=54 pulled=0 p50=16.85s max=30.04s
E       AssertionError: a request naming the faulted source took 30.0s (bound 15.0s)
```

That is the gap reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63602#issuecomment-6491634566: after the in-flight request ends on the 8 s lookup timeout, each new request reconnects and waits on a handshake until `VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (30 s). With #64501 the 7.08 s max is the request that was already in flight when the stop hit.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files (shellcheck, ruff, test tethering).

## Details

- **Why p2p mode only.** In pd mode the decoder waits the full 30 s load timeout while its `remote_prefiller` is stopped, so a time-bound check would fail until that leg has its own fix. The p2p leg is fixed by #64501.
- **No proxy.** `p2p_connector_proxy.py` runs the prefill on the source before calling the decoder, so a stopped source would stall the proxy. The check seeds each source directly and pulls into the decoder with a `remote_kv_source` block, like the #63602 reproducer's probe. A pull counts as a hit when the decoder reports `cached_tokens > 0` (the driver adds `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`); every prefix is unique, so the cached tokens can only have come over the p2p tier.
- **Targeting one instance.** Since #61846 each instance runs in its own session, so the check signals exactly source 0 with `pkill -<SIG> -s <sid>`. A restarted source is started in a new session whose id is written to a file the driver's cleanup reads, so cleanup still stops only this run's processes.
- **Not covered:** RDMA (single-host CI runners have none, so #63498 does not apply), pd mode, and replacing a source at a new address. The kill case restarts on the same ports.
- **CI.** The step `p2p-kv-offload-source-faults-4-gpus` (L4×4, nightly, optional, 30 min) lands commented out, like every step in `disaggregated.yaml` since #63609. The slice needs 3 × 24 GB GPUs; L4 runtime is not measured.
- **Duplicate check.** No open PR adds e2e fault coverage for the P2P tier. #64251 and #64501 are fixes (the latter is what this slice verifies); the #63602 reproducer runs on Kubernetes with RDMA and is not in-tree.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and run the validation. I reviewed the change and the results.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+#
+# Run the p2p tier accuracy + transfer test across a matrix of deployments.
+# One slice per CI step, selected by env var (mirrors
+# tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh):
+#   (default)  dense model: mixed TP, both handshake modes, multi-instance
+#   MLA=1      MLA model with mixed TP (needs ~80 GB GPUs: V2-Lite is 16B)
+#   DP_EP=1    data-parallel / expert-parallel prefillers and decoders
+#   FEATURES=1 cache types beyond plain attention: hybrid Mamba/GDN state,
+#              sliding window, fp8 KV
+#   FAULTS=1   a p2p source stalls, is killed and restarted, or is removed;
+#              asserts time bounds and recovery instead of accuracy
+# Every config sizes for a single 4-GPU host.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
+SCRIPT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/run_accuracy_test.sh"
+
+DENSE_MODEL="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct"
+# deepseek-vl2-tiny is MoE but not MLA (use_mla=false); the smallest real MLA
+# model is DeepSeek-V2-Lite.
+MOE_MODEL="deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny"
+MLA_MODEL="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat"
+# Hybrid GatedDeltaNet + full attention: several KV cache groups plus SSM state.
+HYBRID_MODEL="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"
+# Sliding window of 512 tokens, shorter than the transfer and gsm8k prompts,
+# so out-of-window blocks are actually dropped.
+SWA_MODEL="google/gemma-3-1b-it"
+
+# Mixed prefiller/decoder TP needs CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1: the direct host layout
+# is not byte-identical across TP sizes, so the tier must either refuse the
+# peer (default model runner) or, if it pairs them, hands over unusable KV.
+tp_configs=(
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=p2p MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=p2p CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=2 DECODER_TP_SIZE=1 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  # Direct layout with mixed TP must fall back to recompute until that layout
+  # is byte-portable across TP; flip to a transfer check once it is.
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  EXPECT_TRANSFER=0 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  NUM_PREFILL_INSTANCES=2 NUM_DECODE_INSTANCES=2 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.4 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+)
+# Decoder-first proxy ordering, run as a CLI flag rather than an env knob.
+decoder_first_configs=(
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+)
+mla_configs=(
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 MODEL_NAMES=${MLA_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=p2p CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${MLA_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=2 DECODER_TP_SIZE=1 MODEL_NAMES=${MLA_MODEL}"
+)
+dp_ep_configs=(
+  # P-TP1, D-DPEP=2 (TP=1)
+  "DP_EP=1 P2P_MODE=pd  GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${MOE_MODEL}"
+  # P-TP2, D-DPEP=2 (TP=1)
+  "DP_EP=1 P2P_MODE=p2p CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=2 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${MOE_MODEL}"
+  # P-DP2 (dense replicas), D-TP1: the proxy pins each prefill to a replica
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  PREFILLER_DP_SIZE=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+)
+feature_configs=(
+  "P2P_MODE=p2p MODEL_NAMES=${HYBRID_MODEL}"
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  MODEL_NAMES=${SWA_MODEL}"
+  # fp8 pages through the canonical mixed-TP path that bf16 already covers.
+  "P2P_MODE=pd  CANONICAL_LAYOUT=1 PREFILLER_TP_SIZE=1 DECODER_TP_SIZE=2 VLLM_SERVE_EXTRA_ARGS=--kv-cache-dtype,fp8 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+)
+# Two sources, one decoder, p2p mode; prefiller 0 is the one faulted.
+fault_configs=(
+  "FAULT_CASE=stall  NUM_PREFILL_INSTANCES=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "FAULT_CASE=kill   NUM_PREFILL_INSTANCES=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+  "FAULT_CASE=remove NUM_PREFILL_INSTANCES=2 MODEL_NAMES=${DENSE_MODEL}"
+)
+
+run_tests() {
+  local label=$1
+  local extra_args=$2
+  shift 2
+  local -a configs=("$@")
+
+  echo "=== Running tests (${label}) ==="
+  for cfg in "${configs[@]}"; do
+    local -a cfg_parts extra_args_parts
+    read -r -a cfg_parts <<< "$cfg"
+    read -r -a extra_args_parts <<< "$extra_args"
+
+    echo "-> Running with ${cfg} ${extra_args:+and ${extra_args}}"
+    # 'env' sets the knobs without eval; arrays keep argv splitting SC2086-clean.
+    if ! env "${cfg_parts[@]}" bash "${SCRIPT}" "${extra_args_parts[@]}"; then
+      echo "❌ Test failed for config: ${cfg} ${extra_args:+(${extra_args})}"
+      exit 1
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "✅ All ${label} tests passed!"
+}
+
+cmdline_args=""
+if [[ -n "${ATTENTION_BACKEND:-}" ]]; then
+  echo "ATTENTION_BACKEND is set, running with --attention-backend ${ATTENTION_BACKEND}"
+  cmdline_args="--attention-backend ${ATTENTION_BACKEND}"
+fi
+
+# The selector vars are consumed here; unset them so they do not leak into
+# run_accuracy_test.sh (DP_EP is a knob there too, set per config).
+if [[ -n "${MLA:-}" ]]; then
+  unset MLA
+  run_tests "MLA" "${cmdline_args}" "${mla_configs[@]}"
+elif [[ -n "${DP_EP:-}" ]]; then
+  unset DP_EP
+  run_tests "DP/EP" "${cmdline_args}" "${dp_ep_configs[@]}"
+elif [[ -n "${FEATURES:-}" ]]; then
+  unset FEATURES
+  run_tests "features" "${cmdline_args}" "${feature_configs[@]}"
+elif [[ -n "${FAULTS:-}" ]]; then
+  unset FAULTS
+  run_tests "faults" "${cmdline_args}" "${fault_configs[@]}"
+else
+  run_tests "TP" "${cmdline_args}" "${tp_configs[@]}"
+  run_tests "decoder-first" "${cmdline_args} --decoder-first" \
+    "${decoder_first_configs[@]}"
+fi

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Check that a decoder keeps serving while one of its p2p sources faults.
+
+Two prefillers act as p2p sources and one decoder as the consumer. A probe
+seeds a fresh prefix on each source and then asks the decoder to pull it
+from that source with a ``remote_kv_source`` block, twice a second per source.
+A probe "pulled" when the decoder reports cached prompt tokens for it: the
+prefix is unique, so they can only have come over the p2p tier.
+
+FAULT_CASE picks what happens to source 0 after a healthy baseline:
+    stall   SIGSTOP its processes for STALL_S, then SIGCONT
+    kill    SIGKILL them, then restart it on the same ports
+    remove  SIGTERM them and leave it down
+
+The check asserts time bounds and recovery, not accuracy:
+    - every decoder request returns 200
+    - requests naming the faulted source return within FAULTED_MAX_S, and
+      those sent once the fault has been detected within FAULTED_P50_S at the
+      median: the decoder prefills locally instead of waiting on the source
+    - requests naming the healthy source keep pulling with normal latency,
+      so the fault does not freeze the decoder's p2p control plane
+    - after SIGCONT or the restart, requests naming source 0 pull again
+
+Driven by run_accuracy_test.sh via env vars:
+    TEST_MODEL, FAULT_CASE, DECODE_URL, FAULT_SOURCES (JSON list of
+    {http, host, port, sid, cmd} for source 0 and 1), FAULT_SID_FILE (where
+    a restarted source's session id is appended for the driver's cleanup).
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import random
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import threading
+import time
+import uuid
+
+import requests
+
+MODEL_NAME = os.environ.get("TEST_MODEL", "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct")
+FAULT_CASE = os.environ.get("FAULT_CASE", "stall")
+DECODE_URL = os.environ.get("DECODE_URL", "http://localhost:8200")
+SOURCES = json.loads(os.environ.get("FAULT_SOURCES", "[]"))
+SID_FILE = os.environ.get("FAULT_SID_FILE", "")
+
+PROBE_INTERVAL_S = 0.5
+PROMPT_WORDS = 600
+# A source that is stopped never answers the seed; send the pull regardless.
+SEED_TIMEOUT_S = 3.0
+# Well past VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S (30 s), so a request that waits on
+# the faulted source shows up as a slow 200 rather than a client timeout.
+PULL_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0
+# Give the source time to store the seeded blocks before the pull.
+SEED_TO_PULL_S = 0.3
+
+BASELINE_S = 10.0
+STALL_S = 30.0
+REMOVE_OBSERVE_S = 30.0
+RECOVERY_S = 40.0
+RESTART_READY_TIMEOUT_S = 900.0
+
+# A request that is in flight when the fault hits ends on the tier's 8 s
+# lookup timeout or the 10 s control heartbeat, whichever fires first.
+FAULTED_MAX_S = 15.0
+# Once the heartbeat has caught the fault, a request naming the faulted
+# source must not wait on it at all.
+FAULT_DETECTED_AFTER_S = 12.0
+FAULTED_P50_S = 2.0
+HEALTHY_MAX_S = 5.0
+HEALTHY_MIN_PULLED = 0.9
+BASELINE_MIN_PULLED = 0.5
+# Measured from RECOVERY_GRACE_S after SIGCONT or the restart.
+RECOVERY_GRACE_S = 15.0
+RECOVERY_MIN_PULLED = 0.5
+
+WORDS = [
+    "apple",
+    "river",
+    "cloud",
+    "stone",
+    "forest",
+    "lamp",
+    "ocean",
+    "garden",
+    "silver",
+    "mountain",
+    "candle",
+    "harbor",
+    "meadow",
+    "lantern",
+    "valley",
+    "copper",
+    "willow",
+    "thunder",
+    "desert",
+    "violet",
+]
+
+
+def _prompt(salt: str) -> str:
+    rng = random.Random(salt)
+    return salt + " " + " ".join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(PROMPT_WORDS))
+
+
+def _completion(base: str, prompt: str, timeout: float, **extra) -> dict:
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    try:
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{base}/v1/completions",
+            json={
+                "model": MODEL_NAME,
+                "prompt": prompt,
+                "max_tokens": 1,
+                "temperature": 0,
+                **extra,
+            },
+            timeout=timeout,
+        )
+        status = resp.status_code
+        body = resp.json() if status == 200 else {}
+    except requests.RequestException as exc:
+        status, body = -1, {"error": repr(exc)[:200]}
+    return {"status": status, "lat": time.monotonic() - t0, "body": body}
+
+
+class Probe:
+    """Seeds and pulls a fresh prefix per source every PROBE_INTERVAL_S."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.records: list[dict] = []
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._stop = threading.Event()
+        self._threads: list[threading.Thread] = []
+        self._loop = threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True)
+
+    def start(self) -> None:
+        self._loop.start()
+
+    def stop(self) -> None:
+        self._stop.set()
+        self._loop.join()
+        for th in self._threads:
+            th.join(PULL_TIMEOUT_S + SEED_TIMEOUT_S + 5)
+
+    def _run(self) -> None:
+        next_tick = time.monotonic()
+        while not self._stop.is_set():
+            for idx in range(len(SOURCES)):
+                th = threading.Thread(target=self._one, args=(idx,), daemon=True)
+                th.start()
+                self._threads.append(th)
+            next_tick += PROBE_INTERVAL_S
+            self._stop.wait(max(0.0, next_tick - time.monotonic()))
+
+    def _one(self, idx: int) -> None:
+        src = SOURCES[idx]
+        prompt = _prompt(f"{idx}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}")
+        seed = _completion(src["http"], prompt, SEED_TIMEOUT_S)
+        time.sleep(SEED_TO_PULL_S)
+        t_pull = time.monotonic()
+        pull = _completion(
+            DECODE_URL,
+            prompt,
+            PULL_TIMEOUT_S,
+            kv_transfer_params={
+                "remote_kv_source": {
+                    "kv_request_id": uuid.uuid4().hex,
+                    "remote_host": src["host"],
+                    "remote_port": src["port"],
+                }
+            },
+        )
+        details = (pull["body"].get("usage") or {}).get("prompt_tokens_details")
+        cached = (details or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0
+        with self._lock:
+            self.records.append(
+                {
+                    "src": idx,
+                    "t_pull": t_pull,
+                    "seed_status": seed["status"],
+                    "status": pull["status"],
+                    "lat": pull["lat"],
+                    "pulled": cached > 0,
+                }
+            )
+
+
+def _signal_source(sig: str) -> None:
+    subprocess.run(["pkill", f"-{sig}", "-s", str(SOURCES[0]["sid"])], check=False)
+
+
+def _wait_ready(src: dict) -> None:
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + RESTART_READY_TIMEOUT_S
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        try:
+            if requests.get(f"{src['http']}/health", timeout=2).status_code == 200:
+                return
+        except requests.RequestException:
+            pass
+        time.sleep(1)
+    raise AssertionError(f"restarted source {src['http']} never became ready")
+
+
+def _restart_source() -> None:
+    src = SOURCES[0]
+    # Wait for the killed session to exit so the restart can bind its ports.
+    for _ in range(60):
+        if subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-s", str(src["sid"])]).returncode != 0:
+            break
+        time.sleep(1)
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(["bash", "-c", src["cmd"]], start_new_session=True)
+    if SID_FILE:
+        with open(SID_FILE, "a") as f:
+            f.write(f"{proc.pid}\n")
+    _wait_ready(src)
+
+
+def _window(records, src, start, end=float("inf")):
+    return [r for r in records if r["src"] == src and start <= r["t_pull"] < end]
+
+
+def _pulled_fraction(window) -> float:
+    return sum(r["pulled"] for r in window) / len(window) if window else 0.0
+
+
+def _describe(name, window) -> str:
+    if not window:
+        return f"{name}: no probes"
+    lats = [r["lat"] for r in window]
+    return (
+        f"{name}: n={len(window)} pulled={sum(r['pulled'] for r in window)} "
+        f"p50={statistics.median(lats):.2f}s max={max(lats):.2f}s"
+    )
+
+
+def test_decoder_survives_source_fault():
+    assert FAULT_CASE in ("stall", "kill", "remove"), FAULT_CASE
+    assert len(SOURCES) == 2, "needs a faulted source and a healthy source"
+
+    probe = Probe()
+    t_start = time.monotonic()
+    probe.start()
+    time.sleep(BASELINE_S)
+
+    t_fault = time.monotonic()
+    t_recover = None
+    if FAULT_CASE == "stall":
+        _signal_source("STOP")
+        time.sleep(STALL_S)
+        _signal_source("CONT")
+        t_recover = time.monotonic()
+    elif FAULT_CASE == "kill":
+        _signal_source("KILL")
+        _restart_source()
+        t_recover = time.monotonic()
+    else:
+        _signal_source("TERM")
+        time.sleep(REMOVE_OBSERVE_S)
+    if t_recover is not None:
+        time.sleep(RECOVERY_S)
+    probe.stop()
+
+    records = probe.records
+    fault_end = t_recover if t_recover is not None else float("inf")
+    windows = {
+        "baseline faulted": _window(records, 0, t_start, t_fault),
+        "baseline healthy": _window(records, 1, t_start, t_fault),
+        "fault faulted": _window(records, 0, t_fault, fault_end),
+        "fault healthy": _window(records, 1, t_fault, fault_end),
+    }
+    if t_recover is not None:
+        windows["recovery faulted"] = _window(records, 0, t_recover + RECOVERY_GRACE_S)
+    print(f"\nFAULT_CASE={FAULT_CASE}")
+    for name, window in windows.items():
+        print("  " + _describe(name, window))
+
+    errors = [r for r in records if r["status"] != 200]
+    assert not errors, f"{len(errors)} decoder requests failed, e.g. {errors[0]}"
+
+    for name in ("baseline faulted", "baseline healthy"):
+        assert _pulled_fraction(windows[name]) >= BASELINE_MIN_PULLED, (
+            f"{name}: the probe does not pull over p2p even before the fault"
+        )
+
+    faulted = windows["fault faulted"]
+    assert faulted, "no probes named the faulted source during the fault"
+    worst = max(r["lat"] for r in faulted)
+    assert worst <= FAULTED_MAX_S, (
+        f"a request naming the faulted source took {worst:.1f}s "
+        f"(bound {FAULTED_MAX_S}s)"
+    )
+    detected = [
+        r["lat"] for r in faulted if r["t_pull"] >= t_fault + FAULT_DETECTED_AFTER_S
+    ]
+    assert detected, "the fault window is too short to measure detection"
+    p50 = statistics.median(detected)
+    assert p50 <= FAULTED_P50_S, (
+        f"once the fault was detected, requests naming the faulted source "
+        f"still took p50 {p50:.1f}s (bound {FAULTED_P50_S}s)"
+    )
+
+    healthy = windows["fault healthy"]
+    assert healthy, "no probes named the healthy source during the fault"
+    worst = max(r["lat"] for r in healthy)
+    assert worst <= HEALTHY_MAX_S, (
+        f"a pull from the healthy source took {worst:.1f}s during the fault "
+        f"(bound {HEALTHY_MAX_S}s): the fault stalled the decoder"
+    )
+    assert _pulled_fraction(healthy) >= HEALTHY_MIN_PULLED, (
+        "pulls from the healthy source stopped hitting during the fault"
+    )
+
+    if t_recover is not None:
+        recovered = windows["recovery faulted"]
+        assert _pulled_fraction(recovered) >= RECOVERY_MIN_PULLED, (
+            "pulls from the faulted source did not resume after it came back"
+        )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Check that decoders behind p2p_connector_proxy.py pull KV over the p2p tier.
+
+gsm8k accuracy alone passes even when the decoder silently recomputes the
+prompt, so this sends fully unique prompts through the proxy and asserts the
+decoders' external prefix cache hit counter grew by most of the prompt blocks.
+
+With EXPECT_TRANSFER=0 it asserts the opposite: no KV moved. That pins the
+safe fallback for deployments the tier must refuse (e.g. mixed TP with the
+direct layout), where pairing would hand the decoder unusable bytes.
+
+Driven by run_accuracy_test.sh via env vars:
+    TEST_MODEL, PROXY_URL, DECODE_METRICS_URLS (comma-separated),
+    DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE, EXPECT_TRANSFER.
+"""
+
+import os
+import random
+import time
+import uuid
+
+import openai
+import requests
+from prometheus_client.parser import text_string_to_metric_families
+
+MODEL_NAME = os.environ.get("TEST_MODEL", "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct")
+PROXY_URL = os.environ.get("PROXY_URL", "http://localhost:8192/v1")
+DECODE_METRICS_URLS = os.environ.get(
+    "DECODE_METRICS_URLS", "http://localhost:8200/metrics"
+).split(",")
+BLOCK_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE", "128"))
+NUM_PROMPTS = int(os.environ.get("NUM_TRANSFER_PROMPTS", "8"))
+# Fraction of each prompt's full blocks that must come from the external tier.
+MIN_HIT_FRACTION = 0.5
+EXPECT_TRANSFER = os.environ.get("EXPECT_TRANSFER", "1") == "1"
+HITS_METRIC = "vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits"
+
+WORDS = [
+    "apple",
+    "river",
+    "cloud",
+    "stone",
+    "forest",
+    "lamp",
+    "ocean",
+    "garden",
+    "window",
+    "silver",
+    "bridge",
+    "mountain",
+    "candle",
+    "paper",
+    "engine",
+    "harbor",
+    "violet",
+    "meadow",
+    "castle",
+    "thunder",
+]
+
+
+def _unique_prompt() -> str:
+    # The uuid leads the prompt so no two prompts (or gsm8k prompts) share a
+    # prefix block that the decoder's own GPU prefix cache could serve.
+    tag = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    rng = random.Random(tag)
+    body = " ".join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(5 * BLOCK_SIZE))
+    return f"{tag} {body}"
+
+
+def _external_hits() -> float:
+    total = 0.0
+    for url in DECODE_METRICS_URLS:
+        text = requests.get(url, timeout=30).text
+        for family in text_string_to_metric_families(text):
+            if family.name != HITS_METRIC:
+                continue
+            for sample in family.samples:
+                if sample.name == f"{HITS_METRIC}_total":
+                    total += sample.value
+    return total
+
+
+def test_decoder_pulls_kv_over_p2p():
+    client = openai.OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url=PROXY_URL)
+    before = _external_hits()
+
+    expected_tokens = 0
+    for _ in range(NUM_PROMPTS):
+        completion = client.completions.create(
+            model=MODEL_NAME,
+            prompt=_unique_prompt(),
+            max_tokens=4,
+            temperature=0.0,
+        )
+        assert completion.usage is not None
+        prompt_tokens = completion.usage.prompt_tokens
+        # The last prompt token is always recomputed, so only full blocks
+        # before it can be loaded from the external tier.
+        expected_tokens += (prompt_tokens - 1) // BLOCK_SIZE * BLOCK_SIZE
+
+    assert expected_tokens > 0, "prompts too short to span a full block"
+
+    if not EXPECT_TRANSFER:
+        # Let any late counter update land before asserting nothing moved.
+        time.sleep(5)
+        delta = _external_hits() - before
+        print(f"external prefix cache hits: +{delta:.0f} tokens (expected 0)")
+        assert delta == 0, (
+            f"decoders loaded {delta:.0f} prompt tokens from the external tier "
+            "in a deployment the p2p tier is expected to refuse"
+        )
+        return
+
+    min_hits = MIN_HIT_FRACTION * expected_tokens
+
+    # Counters are published from scheduler stats; give the last step a moment.
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
+    delta = _external_hits() - before
+    while delta < min_hits and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        time.sleep(1)
+        delta = _external_hits() - before
+
+    print(
+        f"external prefix cache hits: +{delta:.0f} tokens "
+        f"(full-block prompt tokens: {expected_tokens}, need >= {min_hits:.0f})"
+    )
+    assert delta >= min_hits, (
+        f"decoders loaded only {delta:.0f} of {expected_tokens} prompt tokens "
+        "from the external tier; KV was recomputed instead of pulled over p2p"
+    )
